sources.entry: Apache Solr - Enterprise search platform featuring full-text search, hit highlighting, faceted search, real-time indexing, dynamic clustering, and rich document (e.g., Word, PDF) handling. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Java/Docker/K8S

summary.one_liner: Apache Solr is an open source, multi-modal search platform built on Apache Lucene, offering full-text, vector, and geospatial search.
summary.what_it_does: Solr is a search server built on Apache Lucene, described in its README as covering full-text, vector, and geospatial search. The README points to a Reference Guide for installation and deployment and to tutorials for deeper introduction. It ships with startup examples via bin/solr start -e, including SolrCloud (cloud), a feature-tour (techproducts), schema-less inference (schemaless), and a films example that adds explicit fields to the _default configset. The README also describes running Solr in Docker via an official image and on Kubernetes via the Solr Operator. Developers build a dev distribution with Gradle (./gradlew dev). The awesome-selfhosted listing describes additional features: hit highlighting, faceted search, real-time indexing, dynamic clustering, and rich document handling such as Word and PDF.
use_cases: indexing PDF and Word files for search
notable: Official Docker image and Kubernetes support via Solr Operator
Built-in example configurations (cloud, techproducts, schemaless, films)
Multi-modal search: full-text, vector, and geospatial
Admin web interface and bin/solr management tool
caveats: README gives no hardware or resource requirements
Installation details are deferred to the external Reference Guide
